te: Land filling and flooding at Wang Noi market, and following up the committee's resolutions
se: The committee considered the complaint about land filling into the Bo Ta Lo canal, Wang Noi district, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya. The province reported that flooding at Wang Noi market comes from filling about 94 rai of private land that used to be low land and a drainage path to Khlong 26, so water can drain only through small pipes in front of the market and cannot cope with heavy rain. The province reported the solutions under way. The meeting then followed up action on the committee's resolutions.
it: Land filling into the Bo Ta Lo canal and flooding at Wang Noi market
Follow-up on the committee's resolutions

te: Following up the return of forest land in Nong Hin, Loei, and the committee's recommendations
se: The meeting noted its findings on buildings of a religious place encroaching on a national reserved forest in Nong Hin district, Loei. The Agricultural Land Reform Office said land reform documents (Sor Por Kor 4-01) there were issued in error because case information was not shared between agencies; it has revoked 6 of 7 and ordered the land returned to the Royal Forest Department. The committee asked the Land Reform Office to find out quickly why documents were issued after a final court ruling, and encouraged officials to follow the law strictly. It then took up the complaint about land filling into the Bo Ta Lo canal, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya.
it: Revoking land reform documents and returning forest land, Nong Hin district, Loei
Land filling into the Bo Ta Lo canal, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya

te: Buildings in a national reserved forest in Nong Hin, Loei
se: The committee considered a complaint about land reform documents and buildings of a religious place inside a national reserved forest in Nong Hin district, Loei. Police and the Office of the PACC said they have taken up the issuing of the documents, and the National Office of Buddhism said it worked with the Royal Forest Department in the area and passed the matter to the local Sangha authorities to check. The committee also took up a complaint about land filling into the Bo Ta Lo canal, Wang Noi district, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya. Complaints are claims that the agencies are still checking.
it: Buildings and land reform documents in a reserved forest, Nong Hin district, Loei
Land filling into the Bo Ta Lo canal, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya

te: Comments on draft amnesty laws for people affected by land and forest policies
se: The committee gave its comments in the public hearing on two draft Amnesty Acts for people affected by state policies on land, forests and natural resources, proposed by members of the House of Representatives. The drafts aim to resolve conflicts between the state and people where state land boundaries overlap homes and farmland, which has led to people being prosecuted.
it: Comments on two draft Amnesty Acts on land, forests and natural resources

te: Following up Khao Siat Ang forest and overlapping areas in Pak Chong
se: The committee continued with encroachment on national reserved forest at Khao Siat Ang, Khao Nok Yung and Khao Ang Hin, Nong Nam Daeng subdistrict, Pak Chong district, Nakhon Ratchasima. It asked about the encroachment and about areas overlapping mining concessions or areas where the Royal Forest Department had allowed use or living inside the reserved forest.
it: Forest encroachment and areas overlapping mining concessions, Pak Chong district, Nakhon Ratchasima

te: Encroachment on national reserved forest in Pak Chong, Nakhon Ratchasima
se: The committee studied encroachment on national reserved forest at Khao Siat Ang, Khao Nok Yung and Khao Ang Hin in Nong Nam Daeng subdistrict, Pak Chong district, Nakhon Ratchasima, with the Natural Resources and Environmental Crime Suppression Division, the Office of the PACC, the Royal Forest Department, the provincial land reform office and the Nakhon Ratchasima land office invited.
it: Encroachment on national reserved forest, Nong Nam Daeng, Pak Chong district

te: Complaint about land documents in the Mae Salit and Pong Daeng forests, Tak
se: The committee looked into claims that land documents were issued wrongly in the Mae Salit and Pong Daeng national reserved forests in Tak. The Royal Forest Department reported on its order 309/2016 on national reserved forest boundaries and on marking the Mae Salit forest boundary with the Department of Lands where the complaint was made. Complaints are claims that the agencies are still checking.
it: Complaint about land documents in the Mae Salit and Pong Daeng forests, Tak

te: Following up seized forest land from durian orchards, and Freedom Beach and Nui Beach in Phuket
se: The committee followed up action under section 25 of the National Reserved Forest Act 1964 on seized land: durian orchards of transnational investors in Chachoengsao, Chanthaburi, Rayong and Trat, and Freedom Beach and Nui Beach in Karon subdistrict, Phuket. The Royal Forest Department said that in Chachoengsao more than 682 rai of forest was encroached and the case has gone to the Department of Special Investigation (DSI), while in Rayong, Chanthaburi and Trat the plots checked have valid title deeds and no forest encroachment for durian was found.
it: Action under section 25 on durian orchards in the East
Seized land at Freedom Beach and Nui Beach, Phuket

te: Security agencies inform the committee on forest encroachment at Ao Chak, Ranong
se: The meeting noted the findings of its study of encroachment on state land and damage to natural resources at Ao Chak, Kamphuan subdistrict, Suk Samran district, Ranong, with the Internal Security Operations Command (ISOC) Region 4, the Fourth Army Area, the Royal Forest Department, the Department of National Parks, Wildlife and Plant Conservation, the Land Development Department, the Department of Lands, the Natural Resources and Environmental Crime Suppression Division and an expert invited.
it: Encroachment on state land at Ao Chak, Ranong (ISOC, Fourth Army Area, land and forest agencies)

te: Highlights for the Senate report, motions received, and land held by nominees for foreigners
se: The committee chose its highlights for the Senate's report and followed up motions sent by the Senate: floods in the North, on which the Land Resources subcommittee has already presented a report on flash floods and mudslides to the Senate; PM2.5 dust, whose draft report is being revised; and plastic waste imports and systematic drought solutions, assigned to the water subcommittee. The meeting also agreed to study land held for foreigners through nominees that affects natural resources, and to visit Sing Buri for a study trip and seminar on the low-carbon city project on 18-19 June 2026.
it: Choosing highlights for the Senate's report
Motions on plastic waste imports and drought
Land held for foreigners through nominees
Study trip and seminar on Sing Buri as a low-carbon city, 18-19 June 2026

te: Draft report on PM2.5 dust, and a shortage of household water in Suphan Buri
se: The meeting considered the draft report of the study on PM2.5 dust in Bangkok, its surrounding provinces and the upper North, and asked the Subcommittee on Climate Change and Air Pollution to complete it, especially the policy proposals on law enforcement, awareness and changing behaviour, and to bring it back. It then took up a complaint about a shortage of water for household use in Hua Na subdistrict, Suphan Buri, with the complainant, the Department of Water Resources and the Department of Groundwater Resources invited.
it: Draft report of the study on PM2.5 dust
Complaint about a shortage of household water, Suphan Buri

te: Progress in revoking land documents at Ao Chak, Ranong
se: The meeting noted progress in revoking land documents issued unlawfully at Ao Chak, Kamphuan subdistrict, Suk Samran district, Ranong, with the Department of Lands and the Department of National Parks, Wildlife and Plant Conservation invited. Through the Ranong subcommittee on proving rights in state land, the Department of Lands checked the land use certificates (Nor Sor 3 Kor) in the target area and reported the background of each plot.
it: Progress in revoking land documents at Ao Chak, Ranong (Department of Lands, national parks department)

te: Royal Forest Department information on land documents over forest at Ao Chak, Ranong
se: The committee continued with the Ao Chak case in Kamphuan subdistrict, Suk Samran district, Ranong. The Royal Forest Department said Laem Son National Park was declared in 1983, land use certificates (Nor Sor 3 Kor) were later issued in the area in 1989-1990, and 21 of them overlap intact forest. A committee set up by the province found these documents unlawful, and trees had been cut in the area, so officials measured and listed the seized timber.
it: Royal Forest Department information on land documents over forest at Ao Chak, Ranong

te: Following up land boundaries and forest encroachment cases at Ao Chak, Ranong
se: The committee continued with the complaint about forest encroachment and land documents at Ao Chak, Suk Samran district, Ranong, with the Department of National Parks, Wildlife and Plant Conservation and other agencies invited to report on checking land boundaries, documents issued over the boundary of Laem Son National Park, legal action, measures to prevent repeat encroachment, handling of seized timber, and progress in revoking land documents.
it: Land boundaries, cases and revoking land documents at Ao Chak, Ranong

te: Complaint about exploring for rock to make cement in Nakhon Nayok
se: The committee heard about a complaint over a project to drill and explore for rock to make cement on the border of Nong Saeng subdistrict, Pak Phli district, and Si Nawa subdistrict, Mueang Nakhon Nayok district. The complainants asked for a check of the exclusive mineral exploration licence in the area, because people worry about effects on natural resources, water sources and the environment. The agencies concerned and the complainants took part. Complaints are claims that the agencies are still checking.
it: Complaint about mineral exploration for cement rock, Nakhon Nayok

te: Forest encroachment and land documents at Ao Chak, Suk Samran, Ranong
se: The committee studied a case of forest encroachment and land documents that may have been issued wrongly at Ao Chak, Kamphuan subdistrict, Suk Samran district, Ranong. Information from the Ranong land office says 16 land use certificates (Nor Sor 3 Kor) in the area were issued in error and unlawfully, because some plots lie in forest.
it: Forest encroachment and land documents at Ao Chak, Ranong
